steps.body: A decimal is just its places, added up. Break 0.375 into what each digit is worth: **3/10 + 7/100 + 5/1000**. That's **expanded form** — the number pulled apart into one piece per place, so you can see exactly where each digit's value comes from.
Shade the same amount in tenths and hundredths.

widget.prompt: Shade 20 hundredths. Watch the grid show that 20/100 is the same amount as 2/10.

commonCounts.feedback: Two cells are 2 hundredths. Two tenths fill two complete columns, or 20 cells.
Ten cells make only 1 tenth. Shade one more full column to reach 2 tenths.

widget.successFeedback: Two full columns are 20 hundredths, or 0.20. The grid proves 2/10 = 20/100.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is less than 20 hundredths. Fill two complete columns.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount is more than 20 hundredths. Stop after two complete columns.

hints: Expanded form takes one digit per place.
The tenths piece is 2/10; the hundredths digit is next.
That digit is 0 — 20 hundredths is exactly two full columns, 2/10.
explanationVariants: 0.20 = 2/10 + 0/100 — shading 20 cells fills exactly two full columns.
20 hundredths is the same amount as 2 tenths: 20/100 = 2/10.

predict.reveal: Cut every tenth into ten slivers and two tenths become twenty hundredths — the amount never moves. That equivalence is what lets expanded form line up.

explanationVariants: Expanded form can use fractions (3/10+7/100+5/1000) or decimals (0.3+0.07+0.005) — same value.
Both forms name each place's piece; the decimal form is just the fraction form written with a point.

steps.body: Expanded form runs both ways. Given the pieces, add them back to rebuild the decimal: 2/10 + 4/100 puts a 2 in tenths and a 4 in hundredths, so it recomposes to **0.24**. Each fraction lands in its own place.

explanationVariants: 2/10 fills tenths with 2, 4/100 fills hundredths with 4: 0.24.
Placing each piece in its place gives 0.24.

commonErrors.feedback: That swaps the places. 2/10 is tenths (first place), 4/100 is hundredths (second): 0.24.
0.6 adds the digits as if same-sized. But tenths and hundredths are different places: 0.24.
6.0 adds 2+4 as whole numbers. These are fractional pieces landing in separate places: 0.24.

widget.successFeedback: 2 in the tenths place, 4 in the hundredths place: 0.24.

steps.body: A number is the sum of its places.
takeaways: Expanded form splits a decimal into one piece per place: 0.375 = 3/10 + 7/100 + 5/1000.
It works in both directions — split apart, or add the pieces back to rebuild the decimal.
An empty place still needs a 0 to hold the other digits in position.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Expanded form writes each digit as its place-piece, then adds them.** In 0.24, the 2 is 2/10 and the 4 is 4/100, so 0.24 = 2/10 + 4/100. One fraction per place, then summed.

explanationVariants: A single-place decimal is one fraction: 0.5 = 5/10.

options.feedback: 5/100 is 0.05, two places. 0.5 has one place: 5/10.
Expanded form uses place-pieces, not the digits added. 0.5 is 5/10.
